rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على ما هداكم is governed by تكبروا. على retains its ordinary sense of elevation because تكبير incorporates the sense of praising God.
rows.anchor: وإنما تعدى فعل التكبير بها لتضمنه معنى الحمد

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases this as magnifying God while praising Him; the Shaykh says this explains meaning, not syntax, since على would then modify the implied حامدين.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا منه تفسير معنى لا إعراب، إذ لو كان كذلك لكان تعلق "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative takes على as لام التعليل; the author prefers its ordinary sense because figurative use of a preposition is weak.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها بمعنى لام العلة، والأول أولى لأن المجاز في الحرف ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is most clearly a verbal noun, meaning His guidance of you; the alternative makes it a relative pronoun and needs an omitted object pronoun and an omitted noun such as following.
rows.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها مصدرية، أي: على هدايته إياكم. والثاني: أنها بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The relative-pronoun parse is remote: it deletes the object هداكموه and needs an omitted noun to yield the sense following what guided you.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وفيه بعد من وجهين، أحدهما: حذف العائد تقديره: هداكموه "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes with hope of gratitude because it follows ease and legal concession; the preceding difficult duties end with hope of piety. The pattern is concessions followed by thanks, unreduced burdens by piety.
rows.anchor: وختمت هذه الآية بترجي الشكر لأن قبلها تيسيرا وترخيصا، فناسب ختمها بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مناسك is the plural of منسك, with either fatḥa or kasra on its second sīn; its derivation was treated shortly before.
rows.anchor: جمع " منسك " بفتح السين وكسرها، وسيأتي تحقيقهما

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: The readers generally pronounce the form distinctly; Abū ʿAmr is reported to assimilate it by treating the inflectional vowel like a building vowel and deleting it. The assimilation occurs here unlike in جباههم and وجوههم.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي عمرو الإدغام، قالوا: شبه الإعراب بحركة البناء فحذفها للإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison kāf works as in كما هداكم, except that the earlier discussion also considered whether it means على or لام.
rows.anchor: إلا في كونها بمعنى " على " أو بمعنى اللام، فليلتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read آباءكم in the accusative as object of the verbal noun, which is annexed to its agent in the regular construction.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على نصب " آباءكم " مفعولا به، والمصدر مضاف لفاعله

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb reads آباؤكم in the nominative, construing the verbal noun as annexed to its object: a son avidly remembers his father.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن كعب: " آباؤكم " رفعا، على أن المصدر مضاف للمفعول

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: A second reading attributed to Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb has the singular أباكم for the generic father; it follows the majority's agent-annexed construction. Nominative case by a dialect treating أباك like a shortened noun is considered remote.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا: " أباكم " بالإفراد على إرادة الجنس، وهي توافق قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: One genitive parse coordinates أشد with the genitive ذكركم under the comparison kāf, estimating like a more intense remembrance; it figuratively makes remembrance itself remember. Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya follow it.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب الزجاج، وتبعه أبو البقاء، وابن عطية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Another genitive parse coordinates أشد with the genitive pronoun in ذكركم: more intense remembrance by you. Its meaning avoids personifying remembrance, but Basran grammarians prohibit coordination on a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله الزمخشري معنى حسن، ليس فيه تجوز بأن يجعل للذكر ذكر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: An accusative parse coordinates أشد with آباءكم, estimating people more intense in remembrance than your fathers; ذكرا is their distinguishing measure, so remembrance is not personified.
rows.anchor: أن يكون معطوفا على " آباءكم " قال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Ibn Jinnī coordinate أشد with the syntactic position of the kāf, understood as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; this figuratively treats remembrance as a rememberer.
rows.anchor: وهذا تخريج أبي علي وابن جني

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī supplies an implicit verb: remember Him with remembrance more intense than your remembrance of your fathers; the verbal noun is an accusative circumstantial description.
rows.anchor: الثالث: قاله مكي: أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار فعل

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies an implicit be: be more intense in remembering God than you are in remembering your fathers, which he considers easier than the figurative parse.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وعندي أن الكلام محمول على المعنى، والتقدير

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: A fifth accusative parse makes أشد a circumstantial modifier of ذكرا, as though it were a delayed adjective; the Shaykh illustrates fronted adjective becoming circumstantial with a line about a desolate trace of Laylā.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أن يكون " أشد " نصبا على الحال من " ذكرا "

words: فَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ ءَابَآءَكُمْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًۭا
rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh says the direct sense is to remember God with remembrance matching or surpassing remembrance of fathers; the five preceding parses are all weak.
rows.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: For the preferred reading, ذكرا may coordinate with the syntactic position of the kāf, though أو is separated from its conjunct by circumstantial أشد. Grammarians permit separation only when the conjunction exceeds one letter and the intervening word is an oath, adverb, or prepositional phrase; the Shaykh treats the circumstance as estimated with a preposition, like an adverb.
rows.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Alternatively, ذكرا is the verbal noun governed by فاذكروا; كذكركم is a fronted circumstance originally adjectival to it, and أشد coordinates with that circumstance.
rows.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual analysis makes ذكرا a specification of degree, but the accusative is puzzling because remembrance is the same kind as the comparison term and would normally be genitive. Earlier parses resolve this by personifying remembrance, making أشد describe persons or a circumstance, or supplying a verb.
rows.anchor: و " ذكرا " تمييز عند غير الشيخ كما تقدم، واستشكلوا كونه تمييزا منصوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes أو as permissive, allowing either way of remembering.
rows.anchor: و " أو " هنا قيل للإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis takes أو as a choice between alternatives.
rows.anchor: وقيل للتخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis takes أو in the sense of بل, rather.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى بل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest parse makes من the subject, with its predicate in the preceding prepositional phrase.
rows.anchor: " من " مبتدأ، وخبره في الجار قبله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows من to function as an agent.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون فاعلة عند الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis treats من as an indefinite noun modified by a descriptive clause.
rows.anchor: وأن تكون نكرة موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing shifts from the preceding pattern: it would have said among you, but من is treated by meaning as plural in our Lord, grant us; agreement with its singular form would be Lord, grant me.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام التفات، إذ لو جرى على النسق الأول لقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second object of آتنا is most clearly omitted for concision or left general: grant us what we want or our request.
rows.anchor: أظهرها: أنه محذوف اختصارا أو اقتصارا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One alternative makes في mean من, yielding grant us from the world; the author rejects it.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن " في " بمعنى " من " أي: من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another alternative treats في as an extra particle, yielding grant us the world; the author rejects it too.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنها زائدة، أي: آتنا الدنيا، وليسا بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr properly denotes grape juice after fermentation and frothing; by metaphor it also covers any other liquid that ferments and froths.
rows.anchor: الخمر: المعتصر من العنب إذا غلى وقذف بالزبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous derivation connects khamr with covering: it veils the mind like a woman's veil. خامري حضاجر is an admonition to a fool to hide; the segment also cites the hadith about covering vessels and poetry using خمر الطريق for concealing vegetation.
rows.anchor: أنها سميت بذلك لأنها تخمر العقل أي تستره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second derivation says wine is covered until it ferments and strengthens, illustrated by the hadith about covering vessels.
rows.anchor: والثاني: لأنها تغطى حتى تدرك وتشتد، ومنه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī derives khamr from its mingling with the mind, as in the phrase the disease mixed with him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري - لأنها تخامر العقل أي: تخالطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth derivation connects khamr with leaving something until it matures, as dough is left to rise or an opinion until its sound course becomes clear. On all four accounts it is originally a verbal noun used for an active or passive participle.
rows.anchor: والرابع: لأنها تترك حتى تدرك، ومنه: " اختمر العجين "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means gambling and is formed on mifʿal from yusr/yasara-yaysiru. Alqama's line uses ييسرون and another poet's uses ييسرونني as usage evidence.
rows.anchor: والميسر: القمار، مفعل من اليسر، يقال: يسر ييسر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participant in drawing lots is called yusr and pluralized as أيسار; another account treats يسر as a plural of ياسر, like حرس from حارس.
rows.anchor: واليسر: الذي يدخل في الضرب بالقداح، ويجمع على أيسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation takes maysir from ease, because winnings are easy to obtain; another derives it from wealth, since gambling strips a person of wealth.
rows.anchor: أحدها: من اليسر وهو السهولة، لأن أخذه سهل. الثاني: من اليسار وهو الغنى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī attributes to Mujāhid a derivation from يسر لي كذا, meaning something became due to me; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it.
rows.anchor: حكاه الطبري عن مجاهد. ورد ابن عطية عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Another derivation links maysir to yasar, slaughtering or cutting: a yāsir is the butcher who divides a camel. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the camel staked for lots was called maysir as the source of gain, then the arrows took that name by proximity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وسميت الجزور التي يستهم عليها ميسرا لأنها موضع اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The draw used ten lots, or eleven in one account: seven bore one through seven marked shares (الفذ، التوءم، الرقيب، الحلس، النافس، المسبل، المعلى); three blanks were المنيح، السفيح، الوغد, with an optional fourth blank called المضعف.
rows.anchor: فالكيفية أن لهم عشرة أقداح وقيل أحد عشر، لسبعة منها حظوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They added blank lots to prevent the impartial dealer (الحرضة) from favoring anyone; he knelt, wrapped himself in a cloth, exposed his head, shook the lots in a bag, and drew one for each named person.
rows.anchor: وإنما كثروا بهذه الأغفال ليختلط على الحرضة وهو الضارب، فلا يميل مع أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A marked lot won its assigned share; a blank meant the person paid toward the camel. This was done in winter scarcity, with the meat given to the poor, not eaten by participants; they took pride in it and called nonparticipants البرم.
rows.anchor: فإن كان من ذوات السهام فاز بذلك النصيب وأخذه، وإن كان من الأغفال غرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most divided the camel into ten portions, one per lot.
rows.anchor: والجزور تقسم عند الجمهور على عدد القداح فتقسم عشرة أجزاء

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the camel was divided by the count of marked lines, producing twenty-eight portions.
rows.anchor: وعند الأصمعي على عدد خطوط القداح، فتقسم على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Aṣmaʿī's division mistaken.
rows.anchor: وخطأ ابن عطية الأصمعي في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls that correction surprising: Arabs may have divided the camel by ten lots on one occasion and by twenty-eight marked shares on another.
rows.anchor: وهذا عجيب منه، لأنه يحتمل أن العرب كانت تقسمها مرة على عشرة ومرة على ثمانية وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noun is omitted after عن: the question concerns the ruling on wine and gambling, including permissibility or prohibition, not the substances themselves; the answer matches that understood question.
rows.anchor: وقوله { عن الخمر } لا بد من حذف مضاف، إذ السؤال عن ذاتي الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيهما is the fronted predicate and إثم the delayed subject. Fronting is optional because indefiniteness is also licensed by description or coordination; a noun meaning their use is omitted because sin is not inherent in the substances.
rows.anchor: الجار خبر مقدم، و " إثم " مبتدأ مؤخر، وتقديم الخبر هنا ليس بواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read كثير; the others read كبير. The majority form suits sin described as grave, drinking and gambling as major sins, and the seven readers' ب in وإثمهما أكبر.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة الكسائي: " كثير " بالثاء المثلثة، والباقون بالباء ثانية الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The much-sin reading may describe the many individual sins of drinkers and gamblers, or the repeated and multiplied punishment resulting from their acts.
rows.anchor: وأما وجه قراءة الأخوين: فإما باعتبار الآثمين من الشاربين والمقامرين فلكل واحد إثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also encompass the bad words and deeds produced by drinking, and all involved with wine from grape to consumption; the Prophet cursed wine and ten parties connected with it.
rows.anchor: وإما باعتبار ما يترتب على شربها مما يصدر من شاربها من الأقوال السيئة والأفعال القبيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural benefits contrasts with singular sin, so describing the sin as many matches the collective sense. The author says each reading should be supported without weakening the other, as in the earlier ملك and مالك discussion.
rows.anchor: مقابل ل " منافع " و " منافع " جمع، فناسب أن توصف مقابلة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls the ب reading better: grave sins are called كبائر and lesser ones صغائر. He still regards the ث reading as sound, since abundance is a kind of greatness just as smallness can mean lowliness or scarcity.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " الأحسن القراءة بالباء لأنه يقال: إثم كبير وصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This opening was discussed at the parallel expression in 2:243; ʿAlī is reported to read تر with a still rāʾ, whose analysis was also given there.
rows.anchor: تقدم نظيره في قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ربه most clearly refers to Abraham; another analysis refers it to the disputant.
rows.anchor: والهاء في " ربه " فيهما قولان، أظهرهما: أنها تعود على " إبراهيم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاجه means that he displayed rivalry in argument with Abraham, trying to prevail through his proof.
rows.anchor: ومعنى حاجه: أظهر المغالبة في حجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest parse makes أن آتاه a causal object with a deleted preposition, because God gave him kingship. It can then be accusative or genitive; the preposition is omitted because this cause clause lacks the same subject, a deletion allowed with لام before أن.
rows.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه مفعول من أجله على حذف حرف العلة، أي: لأن آتاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One causal interpretation is ironic reversal: the man should have thanked God for kingship but instead made it an occasion for disputation, like the reversal in 56:82 and the example of opposing someone because he treated you well.
rows.anchor: أنه من باب العكس في الكلام بمعنى أنه وضع المحاجة موضع الشكر، إذ كان من حقه أن يشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other causal interpretation is that receiving kingship made him arrogant and insolent, which led to his dispute with Abraham.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن إيتاء الملك حمله على ذلك، لأنه أورثه الكبر والبطر، فتسبب عنهما المحاجة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead lets أن and its clause function as a time expression: he disputed when God gave him kingship. The Shaykh questions this because the dispute was not simultaneous with the grant unless time is loose, and notes grammarians' objection to a clause replacing a temporal noun; he counters that maṣdariyya ما can do so.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يكون التقدير: حاج وقت أن آتاه "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in آتاه most clearly refers to the disputant; al-Mahdawī allows Abraham as referent, taking the gift as the kingship of prophecy. Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls that interpretation forced.
rows.anchor: والضمير في " آتاه " فيه وجهان، أحدهما - وهو الأظهر - أن يعود على " الذي "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh identifies the Abraham-as-recipient reading as Muʿtazilite: kingship is a divine covenant that wrongdoers cannot receive (2:124), while 4:54 says Abraham's family received scripture, wisdom, and great kingship.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " هذا قول المعتزلة، قالوا: لأن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest governor of إذ قال is حاج: he disputed when Abraham said this.
rows.anchor: قوله: { إذ قال } فيه أربعة أوجه، أظهرها: أنه معمول لحاج

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ makes إذ depend on آتاه; the author questions this because granting kingship was not the time Abraham made his statement, except by loose extension of the time phrase.
rows.anchor: ذكره أبو البقاء. وفيه نظر من حيث إن وقت إيتاء الملك ليس وقت قول إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows إذ as appositive to أن آتاه if that clause means at the time; the author considers this weak because the time expressions differ unless construed loosely. Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects apposition if أن is causal, unless إذ itself means the verbal noun أن, an attested usage.
rows.anchor: أجازه الزمخشري بناء منه على أن " أن " واقعة موقع الظرف

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī makes إذ depend on تر, but the author rejects this: seeing, on either interpretation of the parallel expression, did not occur when Abraham said this.
rows.anchor: ذكره مكي، وهذا ليس بشيء، لأن الرؤية على كلا التفسيرين المذكورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربي is a subject with a relative-clause predicate, and the whole clause is governed in the accusative by قال; أنا أحيي is likewise a subject-predicate clause governed by قال.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر في محل نصب بالقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham states God's power through a relative clause, which implies exclusivity; the disputant's finite clause does not. He did not claim unique possession of that lowly power for himself.
rows.anchor: وأخبر عن " أنا " بالجملة الفعلية، وعن " ربي " بالموصول بها، لأنه في الإخبار بالموصول يفيد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنا is a separate nominative pronoun; its underlying form is أن, with added alif to mark the vowel at pause and ordinarily deleted in connected speech. Some retain it throughout, explained either by extending pause pronunciation into liaison or by dialect.
rows.anchor: و " أنا " ضمير مرفوع منفصل، والاسم منه " أن "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound account recognizes two dialects: Tamīm retains alif in both pause and liaison, which explains Nāfiʿ's reading before hamza with ḍamma or fatḥa and his differing report before kasra, and Ibn ʿĀmir's form noted later. The other dialect retains alif only at pause; liaison retention is poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنه فيه لغتان، إحداهما: لغة تميم، وهي إثبات ألفه وصلا ووقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other forms are أنا, أن, and آن; one account explains آن by moving alif before nūn and associates it with time. In أنه, the hāʾ is pause hāʾ rather than a substitute for alif, as cited poetry illustrates.
rows.anchor: وفيه لغات: أنا وأن - كلفظ أن الناصبة - وآن، وكأنه قدم الألف على النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ retains alif before hamza either by combining the two dialects or because hamza is difficult to pronounce and the long vowel eases it.
rows.anchor: وإنما أثبت نافع ألفه قبل الهمز جمعا بين اللغتين، أو لأن النطق بالهمز عسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ answers an omitted condition: Abraham effectively says if you claim or pretend that, then God... Without the omitted condition, a quotation after قال would have no fāʾ and would read قال إبراهيم إن الله يأتي.
rows.anchor: هذه الفاء جواب شرط مقدر تقديره: قال إبراهيم إن زعمت أو موهت بذلك

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the fāʾ connects the statement to what preceded: if the opponent claims life and death without understanding, the proof is that God brings the sun.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " دخلت الفاء إيذانا بتعلق هذا الكلام بما قبله، والمعنى إذا أدعيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in بالشمس makes the verb transitive: أتت الشمس means the sun came, while أتى الله بها means He brought it; من المشرق and من المغرب modify their respective verbs.
rows.anchor: والباء في " بالشمس " للتعدية، تقول: أتت الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows the directional phrases as circumstances meaning subjugated or compliant, after previously denying that analysis; the author wishes he had maintained his initial rejection.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء فيهما بعد أن منع ذلك أن يكونا حالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read بهت passively: الذي is raised as the passive subject, with Abraham as the understood agent; alternatively, the original agent may be the speech implied by قال.
rows.anchor: الجمهور: " بهت " مبنيا للمفعول، والموصول مرفوع به

rows.speaker: ابن السميفع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ reads بهت with fatḥa on both consonants as active: Abraham may be subject and the disbeliever object, meaning Abraham defeated him in argument; alternatively the disbeliever is subject and Abraham an omitted object as the disbeliever resorted to slander when silenced.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: " فبهت " بفتح الباء والهاء مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ's active reading, an intransitive parse takes الذي as subject, matching the passive reading's meaning of bewilderment; it can also mean to produce a falsehood.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون لازما والموصول فاعل، والمعنى معنى بهت

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads fatḥa on bāʾ and ḍamma on hāʾ with the relative pronoun as subject; al-Akhfash reports a kasra on hāʾ, also intransitive. The author summarizes three forms: both fatḥa, ḍamma, and kasra; the fatḥa form can be transitive or intransitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: " فبهت " بفتح الباء وضم الهاء كظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بهت means bewilderment and astonishment; bāhata or bahtahu can mean confronting someone with a lie. The cited saying calls the Jews people of falsehood because lies bewilder the person lied to.
rows.anchor: والبهت: التحير والدهش، وباهته وبهته واجهه بالكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lie confounds the person against whom it is directed, explaining the use of بهت for bewilderment.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الكذب يحير المكذوب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse attaches في الأرض directly to يخفى.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " يخفى "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, في الأرض modifies an omitted adjective describing شيء.
rows.anchor: وأن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة لشيء
